titleEn: Thomas Duffy: Can electric tractors compete with diesel on Irish farms?
titleZh: 电动拖拉机能否在爱尔兰农场上与柴油机一较高下？
summaryZh: 本文探讨了电动拖拉机在爱尔兰农业中的可行性，对比了电动与柴油在能量效率、续航、充电时间及成本上的差异。作者指出，尽管电动拖拉机效率更高，但受限于充电速度、电网基础设施（尤其是爱尔兰农场缺乏三相电）以及高购机成本，目前难以替代柴油机。文章还介绍了可更换电池等创新方案，为未来农业机械电动化提供了参考。
contentFull: Top Stories Beef Dairy Sheep Tillage Machinery Northern Ireland Videos Podcasts Top Stories Beef Dairy Sheep Tillage Machinery Northern Ireland Videos Podcasts Thomas Duffy: Can electric tractors compete with diesel on Irish farms? ![Image 1: Thomas Duffy By Thomas Duffy August 29, 2026 10:00 AM](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsauthorthomas-duffy) Share this article ![Image 2: Can electric tractors offer a real alternative to diesel?](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsthomas-duffy-can-electric-tractors-compete-with-diesel-on-irish-farms) Can electric tractors offer a real alternative to diesel? Government supports and high fuel costs appear to have spurred on a wave of electric car purchases in Ireland, according to latest figures. For farming, however, is there any real alternative to offset the similar increase in fuel price? There remain only three alternatives to diesel on the dealers lot for most Irish field work, Fendt’s e107 Vario and New Holland’s T6.180 and T7.270 methane tractors. All three carry a hefty price tag but the larger drawback to all three remains refuelling and running time. Unless you have a personal biodigester methane-powered tractors will require a trip to a specialist CNG refuelling station so infield refuelling is out. Electric tractors Electric tractors however do have a ready resupplying source in every socket - the issue instead is speed of recharging. The largest issue with knocking diesel from its throne in agriculture is that unlike with electric cars you cannot overcome shorter ranges with more chargers. Not only do field tractors require long run times but more importantly suffer short windows to refuel. Even without considering contractor jobs such as silage - which depending on even tighter weather windows and often a 24-hour job only stopping minutes to refuel driver and machine - farmer demands are far higher than most car users. Crunching the numbers on fuel use is challenging as everything from soil type to weather conditions can vary consumption. Interestingly emissions management systems such as DPF and adblue, along with more transmission consumption because of its complexity, have undone a lot of the efficiency gains in the internal combustion engine. This means that often 30-year-old machines use as much per hour as those rolling off the forecourt. Speaking with the operators of newer machines on a sample of work gives anywhere from 20L to 180L per hour for various jobs from topping to pumping slurry. A sample job such as ploughing alone can vary from 40L to 80L per hour. For a demonstration of the challenges facing electric tractors, we can take the example of a job which normally consumes 60L per hour of field work. Considering how much electricity is needed to replace this, we need to convert those 60ltrs into energy units (kWh). Handily a litre is equivalent to 10.7kWh in stored capacity. For convenience we will round this down to 10kWh to account for some variables, meaning our 60Lhour means 600kWh roughly 6 times that of the storage of the Fendt e107. Super power Here is where electric tractors have a super power - efficiency. Diesel is a very efficient dense way to transport energy. The same 10kWh in lithium batteries would be 60-80kg vs diesel’s 0.85kg, but getting that power out is extremely inefficient. Even the most efficient tractor engines will only get approximately 35% of the stored power per litre losing the remainder to friction and majority to heat. We do not yet have public figures for the efficiency of the on the market electric tractors but comparing car EVs to their diesel counterparts shows an efficiency of grid energy to kms is close to 70%. If we take this figure then that energy requirement falls to 300kWh. In theory, this means our 100kWh tractor would require recharging after roughly 20 minutes. Fendt, as the first out, says however their aim is not this form of field work but rather smaller jobs where run time could be more realistic. Recharging But then recharging is where it gets really tricky. If you happen to be right beside an EV fast charger (80kWh), this electric tractor can recharge fully in a little over an hour. Charging on a more realistic set-up in yard of 22kw on 3-phase means it will take just under five hours. Unfortunately this runs into a different issue; while most continental farms have 3-phase as standard, Irish farms do not, meaning they are limited to 7kw or lengthy 14hrs charge time for approximately 20 minutes' work. That poses the question: if our EV tractor has such limitations will diesel ever have a real competitor? Perhaps some would argue not in its standard formation, but there are companies which are currently working on ideas. Two startups in the tractor space are squaring up to the legacy makers by using the innovative idea of swappable batteries. The idea may not be as outlandish as it sounds – just look at the efforts that were made to overcome the issues of slow charging in Chinese HGVs. translationZh:
政府支持和燃料成本高企似乎推动了爱尔兰电动汽车购买量的增长，根据最新数据。然而，对于农业来说，是否存在真正的替代方案来抵消燃料价格的类似上涨？在经销商处，对于大多数爱尔兰田间作业，柴油的替代品只有三种：芬特e107 Vario以及纽荷兰T6.180和T7.270甲烷拖拉机。这三款都价格不菲，但更大的缺点是加油和运行时间。除非你拥有个人沼气池，否则甲烷动力拖拉机需要前往专门的CNG加气站，因此田间加油是不可能的。

**电动拖拉机**

然而，电动拖拉机确实有现成的补给源——每个插座，问题在于充电速度。将柴油从农业王座上拉下来的最大问题是，与电动汽车不同，你不能通过增加充电桩来克服续航短的问题。田间拖拉机不仅需要长时间运行，更重要的是加油时间窗口很短。即使不考虑承包商工作（如青贮饲料——这取决于更紧张的天气窗口，通常24小时工作，仅停几分钟给司机和机器加油），农民的需求也远高于大多数汽车用户。

计算燃料使用量颇具挑战性，因为从土壤类型到天气条件等一切因素都会影响消耗。有趣的是，排放管理系统（如DPF和AdBlue）以及由于复杂性而增加的传动系统消耗，已经抵消了内燃机效率提升的很大一部分。这意味着，30年前的机器每小时消耗的燃料往往与刚出厂的新机器一样多。与新型机器的操作员交谈，从割草到抽泥浆等各种工作，每小时消耗从20升到180升不等。例如，犁地这样的示例工作每小时消耗可能在40升到80升之间。

为了展示电动拖拉机面临的挑战，我们可以举一个例子：一项通常每小时消耗60升柴油的田间作业。要计算需要多少电力来替代，我们需要将这60升转换为能量单位（千瓦时）。方便的是，一升柴油相当于10.7千瓦时的存储容量。为了方便，我们将其向下取整为10千瓦时以考虑一些变量，这意味着我们每小时60升的消耗相当于600千瓦时，大约是芬特e107存储容量的6倍。

**超级动力**

这就是电动拖拉机的超级动力——效率。柴油是一种非常高效、密集的能源运输方式。同样的10千瓦时，锂电池重60-80公斤，而柴油仅重0.85公斤，但提取这些能量却极其低效。即使最高效的拖拉机发动机，每升存储能量的利用率也仅为约35%，其余损失于摩擦，大部分以热量形式散失。我们还没有公开市场上电动拖拉机的效率数据，但将电动汽车与其柴油对应车型进行比较，电网能量到行驶里程的效率接近70%。如果我们采用这个数字，那么能量需求将降至300千瓦时。理论上，这意味着我们100千瓦时的拖拉机大约每20分钟就需要充电。芬特作为先行者，表示他们的目标不是这种田间作业，而是运行时间更现实的小型作业。

**充电**

但充电才是真正棘手的地方。如果你恰好靠近一个电动汽车快速充电桩（80千瓦），这款电动拖拉机可以在一个多小时内充满电。在农场院子里使用更现实的22千瓦三相电设置，则需要近5小时。不幸的是，这遇到了另一个问题：虽然大多数欧洲大陆的农场标配三相电，但爱尔兰农场并非如此，这意味着他们只能使用7千瓦的充电功率，或者长达14小时的充电时间，而只能工作约20分钟。

这就引出了一个问题：如果我们的电动拖拉机有如此限制，柴油还会有真正的竞争对手吗？也许有人会认为，在其标准形态下不会，但有些公司正在研究解决方案。拖拉机领域的两家初创公司正通过可更换电池的创新理念向传统制造商发起挑战。这个想法可能并不像听起来那么离谱——看看中国为克服重型卡车慢充问题所做的努力吧。
